candidates.title: Map changing CRM items into invoice rows

demandEvidence.chore: Map a changing number of CRM item values into invoice rows for an external system.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I cannot map array data for dynamic amount of invoice rows to the HTTP POST module’s “invoice rows” section.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable table that converts each supplied CRM item into one proposed invoice row, with uncertain mappings flagged.
inputs: Synthetic CRM record with item description and quantity
Synthetic unit price and tax category supplied by an operator
Operator-written mapping rules for the fictional invoice API
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a batch after supplying fictional CRM records and approved mapping rules.
steps: Read the supplied fictional CRM fields and mapping rules.
Propose one invoice row for each supplied item using only the provided values.
Flag missing or ambiguous fields instead of guessing.
Compare the proposed row count with the supplied item count.
Show the draft table to an operator for correction and approval.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a small synthetic record with multiple items, verify that the draft contains the same number of rows, preserves each supplied quantity and price, and flags an intentionally missing mapping.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies and approves mapping rules, checks every row and amount, and handles any real accounting system entry. Do not send requests, persist invoices, calculate tax, or use live customer data.
unverified: No supplied reference documents dynamic array mapping into an HTTP POST invoice payload.
No evidence establishes external endpoint behavior or invoice persistence.
Tax correctness and the business's field mapping are unverified.
Any AI-assisted extraction or workflow execution is untested.

ease.reason: A student can prototype a table from fictional records, but no supplied reference supports dynamic invoice-row mapping or HTTP payload construction.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service firms that prepare invoices might pay for row preparation; this forum question establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic-data table test is narrow, while API mapping, invoice persistence and tax behavior remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed draft can flag gaps and compare row counts, but no execution capability is documented and an operator must verify every row.

evidence.reason: The original post gives a concrete variable invoice-row mapping problem and sample CRM arrays, but no recurrence or corroborating demand evidence.

candidates.reason: Concrete task assessed as a proposed synthetic-data row-drafting experiment. Its provisional mean is 4.2, below threshold; supplied Make error-handling documentation does not support array mapping, external endpoint execution, or invoice persistence.
